reason: E1 states the rationale for adding 0.1 at.% B to HfMoNbTaTiZr to precipitate borides and improve grain-boundary cohesion. E2 and E3 directly report the resulting intergranular (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitation, the change in fracture mode, and the measured increase in fracture strain from 12.3% to 19.3% with only a slight yield strength increase. However, none of the cited evidence addresses impact-induced energy release, so that premise is unsupported.
premises: Boron addition induces intergranular (Hf,Zr)B2 precipitation in HfMoNbTaTiZr
Enhanced cohesion changes fracture from intergranular to transgranular
This improves ductility (fracture strain ~12% to ~19%) without significant strength loss
Impact-induced energy release is maintained relative to undoped alloy
